---
title: "Sensitivity to costs, weights and grade restrictions"
subtitle: "4.10 · settings and sensitivity after the postrank vignette a7"
description: "How withholding costs, criterion weights and grade caps change a report."
---

Changing the withholding cost or the criterion weights changes how the report is evaluated. Changing the
grade cap changes which reports may be chosen.

```{=html}
<div id="app" class="prx-app column-page"></div>
<script src="../../js/vendor/d3.min.js"></script>
<script src="../../js/vendor/plot.min.js"></script>
<script src="../../js/bundles/choosing-settings.js"></script>
<script>window.__prxApp = PRX["choosing-settings"].mountWidget(document.getElementById("app"));</script>
```

For the live path, we vary the withholding cost while holding the posterior, weights and available reports
fixed. The grid repeats the comparison for the listed combinations of costs, caps and weights. We use the
criterion error shares and number of stated pairs to compare what the reports say as settings change.
The archived cases provide results at the recorded settings.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Equal weights.** The best report states 9 of 15 pairs. Its wrong shares are .0177 and .0267 on scores A and B.
  The exact path gives its interval and all returned equal-risk alternatives at the boundary costs.
- **A higher price.** The report states 11 pairs; score B’s wrong share is .115. A larger withholding cost can favor additional statements, even though some statements are less certain.
- **A still higher price.** The report states 12 pairs, while score B’s wrong share falls to .0575. Disclosure
  cannot fall along this fixed-family exact path; a criterion-specific wrong share can move either way.
- **At most two grades.** The best report states 8 pairs with risk .0939. The cap table holds the price and weights fixed. A higher cap retains every previously allowed report,
  so the minimum risk can only stay the same or fall.
- **Thirty-site archive.** Recorded disclosures include 131, 276, 305 and 312 pairs. These dots describe the saved
  solves at their recorded prices. Their spacing does not locate the exact transitions of a continuous path.
- **Tutorial archive.** The package’s prepared sensitivity analysis has 7 settings, changing one setting at a time.
  In the live grid, we evaluate a fixed reference report under every combination.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
Each row reevaluates the reference report under that row's loss, even when the cap rules it out of the search.
The thirty-site archives use joint posterior draws and fixed settings. The live Gaussian example gives the
intervals and boundary reports along its path. The archive points show the original solver status and gap.
The R example reads the tutorial results, which vary one setting at a time.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="In postrank"}
```r
library(postrank)
s <- readRDS(system.file("extdata/cached/tutorial_sensitivity.rds", package="postrank", mustWork=TRUE))$value
s$table[, c("setting_id", "risk", "N")]
```
:::

Standalone: [choosing-settings](../../embed/choosing-settings.html), for example `?preset=tau40&theme=dark`.
